headline: The New Milford starter.
subhead: Key landmarks, parks, and routes across town. Swipe.

slides.title: The Town Green
slides.text: One of the longest in Connecticut. It hosts the bandstand, seasonal events, and the annual tree lighting every holiday season.

slides.title: Lovers Leap State Park
slides.text: Known for its 1895 red iron bridge, walking trails, and direct views over the Housatonic River gorge.

slides.title: Candlewood Lake Access
slides.text: Lynn Deming Park provides town residents with lake swimming, a public boat launch, docks, and picnic areas.

slides.title: Historic Bank Street
slides.text: A walkable downtown stretch with brick sidewalks, independent storefronts, and the long-standing local movie theater.

slides.title: Route 7 Corridor
slides.text: The main north-south artery connecting town directly south to Brookfield, Danbury, and Interstate 84.

slides.title: Harrybrooke Park
slides.text: A private, non-profit park open to the public, featuring paved loops along the Still River and wooded walking trails.

If you are researching New Milford CT, start with the core spots. Bank Street anchors the downtown business district with brick sidewalks, and Route 7 handles the commute straight down to Danbury.
